title: Confined space entry — fire water tanks, pump wells, pits and risers
verdict:
I would not sign this. It is a better document than the one it replaces — all eight of the previous round's findings are genuinely answered, not gestured at — but it makes one promise it cannot keep, and a crew that believes that promise will take an entry with no rescue in it.

WHAT IS FIXED, AND I CHECKED EACH ONE. The ignition gap is closed properly: steps[10].controls[0] puts solvent lining and re-coating out of scope entirely, steps[10].controls[3] is a real ignition control naming s 73 in the control text with Ex ia certification, the blower motor out of the vapour path, bonding and earthing of drums and spray gear, and withdrawal at 5% LEL as a house rule stricter than s 72(2); steps[10].controls[2] now says out loud that battery, ELV, IP and RCD are shock and water controls and nothing else. The structural gap is closed by a new steps[4] that is the best-written step in the file — the dividing-wall HOLD POINT, the vent proven clear by looking through it, a drain rate the tank can breathe at, the structural walk-around, and where the discharge goes. The two hierarchy mislabels are fixed and, better than fixed, explained: steps[9].controls[6] is now ppe and says why under s 79(3)(c), steps[5].controls[9] names restraint as a work positioning system under s 79(3)(b). The opening measurement is administrative and sits below the engineering controls. The gas-testing set is in the steps[0] load-out with the hose draw time on the permit. training[10] is corrected to CPCCWHS1001 — confirmed on training.gov.au, Release 1, replacing CPCCOHS1001A. The s 37 and BFSR s 49 overstatements are both repaired, the latter now reading "if a fire or hazardous materials emergency happens", which is the section's exact wording.

CITATIONS. I pulled the WHS Regulation 2011 (Qld), the Building Fire Safety Regulation 2008 (Qld), the Electrical Safety Act 2002 (Qld) and the Electrical Safety Regulation 2026 (Qld) in force today and read the sections. The two new citations are both right: s 78(2)(b) is "in the vicinity of an opening through which a person could fall" and s 78(2)(d) is "on a surface through which a person could fall" — a tank roof is genuinely both — and s 79(3) ranks (a) fall prevention device, (b) work positioning system, (c) fall arrest system exactly as the document states. s 73 is quoted accurately. s 67(4), s 72(2), s 74(3)(a)(b)(c), s 75(2)(3), s 76(2), s 77(2)(3), s 291(a)(d)(f)(k)(l)(n)(o)(q) and s 299(4) all say what the document says they say. ESR 2026 Part 8 is "Electrical work" and its Division 3 is "Electrical work on or near energised electrical equipment" at s 193 — correct. BFSR s 53 puts the 24-hour critical defect notice on the person who carried out the maintenance, and the pump-defect example is the Regulation's own. ES Act s 18(1)(b) includes testing an installation. The repealed 2013 regulation appears once, beside its replacement, correctly. I did not re-verify the Australian Standard editions or the Code of Practice years this round; the document hedges AS/NZS 60079 and the asbestos code honestly, which is the right instinct.

BUILD RULES. Clean. Fourteen steps, six keys each, no control out of hierarchy order, no residual above its initial, and neither low-residual step (steps[0], steps[11]) rests on administrative and PPE alone.

WHY I AM NOT SIGNING. The rescue is "on-site no-entry retrieval by the standby on the rigged winch" for every entry, and entry rescue is forbidden without an air set the three-person crew does not carry. A winch over a hatch recovers a person who is under the hatch. A fire water tank is a horizontal space — the entrant walks the floor to a tie rod or a panel joint — and steps[10].controls[9] and steps[10].hazards both contemplate the entrant being out of the standby's sight. Nothing in fourteen steps limits how far the entrant may work from the retrieval point, requires the line to stay connected or to reach the furthest work position, or says what happens when the casualty is lying eight metres from the opening. siteSpecificPrompts[0] collects the internal dimensions and nothing ever uses them. Two further faults sit under it: steps[6].controls[3] runs the blower for twenty minutes "before the first atmospheric test", so the one piece of plant the document itself names as an ignition source starts on an atmosphere nobody has read and three steps before the ignition control exists — and that contradicts steps[1].controls[2], which says the atmosphere is tested from outside whenever the opening is open. And steps[4].controls[1] sends the crew to crack a hatch on a full tank, which is the exact act steps[6].controls[10] exists to control, without pointing at it — in a control that already points forward correctly for the vent check. Fix those three and the rest is signable; it is written by somebody who has been in these tanks.

blocking.field: steps[8].controls[8] ("The rescue plan for every entry is on-site no-entry retrieval by the standby on the rigged winch"), with steps[8].controls[0], steps[8].hazards and steps[10].controls[9]
blocking.problem: THE RESCUE THIS DOCUMENT GUARANTEES DOES NOT EXIST FOR A HORIZONTAL SPACE, AND THE DOCUMENT NEVER SAYS SO. steps[8].controls[8] commits absolutely: 'The rescue plan for every entry is on-site no-entry retrieval by the standby on the rigged winch, written on the permit.' The emergency section then forbids the alternative — 'DO NOT SEND A SECOND PERSON IN AFTER THE FIRST', and nobody enters for rescue 'without air supplied respiratory equipment they are fit-tested for, their own standby outside, and the same controls that applied to the original entry' — which the mandated three-person crew does not carry unless the space happened to need an air set. A tripod and winch over a hatch retrieves a person who is under the hatch. A fire water tank is not a shaft: the entrant walks across the floor to a tie rod, a panel joint, the anti-vortex plate or the strainer, and the document knows it — steps[10].controls[9] says the standby 'keeps the entrant in sight where the space allows it and in continuous voice contact where it does not', and steps[10].hazards names 'Entrant becoming unwell out of the standby's sight'. Nothing anywhere limits how far the entrant may work from the retrieval point, requires the retrieval line to stay connected after steps[8].controls[0] ('connect the retrieval line before the entrant's feet leave the ground'), requires the line to be long enough to reach the furthest work position — the only length in the document is a '15m rescue line' in the steps[0] load-out, tied to nothing — requires the tripod or opening to be repositioned over the work, or offers any rescue at all for a casualty lying eight metres from the hatch. steps[8].controls[2] measures the opening and never the geometry behind it. siteSpecificPrompts[0] collects 'depth and internal dimensions' and no control ever uses them. So a crew reads a statement that promises a rescue for every entry, signs a permit that records that rescue, and enters a space where the promise is void the moment the entrant steps off the line of the hatch. That is the fault that kills people in tanks.
blocking.fix: Add an administrative HOLD POINT to steps[8], below controls[2]: the retrieval line stays connected for the whole entry, and the entrant does not work beyond the point from which the standby can wind them back to the opening on it. Write the furthest work position, the line length and the distance from the opening on the permit alongside the opening dimensions. Where the work is beyond that reach — a horizontal tank run, an internal wall, a baffle, a bend in a riser — the entry does not proceed as a no-entry retrieval: either reposition the opening and the tripod so the work sits under it, or the job is planned as an entry rescue with a second fit-tested air-set rescuer and their own standby named on the permit, and the crew is bigger than three. Add 'casualty down away from the opening, out of reach of the winch line' to steps[8].hazards, and add a matching prompt to siteSpecificPrompts asking how far the work is from the retrieval point.

blocking.field: steps[6].controls[3] (level "engineering", "Purge for at least 20 minutes before the first atmospheric test"), with steps[6].controls[4] and steps[1].controls[2]
blocking.problem: THE BLOWER RUNS FOR TWENTY MINUTES ON AN ATMOSPHERE NOBODY HAS READ, AND THE IGNITION CONTROL IS THREE STEPS AWAY. steps[6].controls[3] states the order plainly: 'Purge for at least 20 minutes before the first atmospheric test.' So the first piece of plant to run at the opening runs before any oxygen, LEL or CO reading exists. The word 'intrinsic' does not appear anywhere in steps[5], steps[6] or steps[7]; s 73 appears only at steps[10].controls[3], inside the step titled 'Do the work inside the space' and scoped to what 'goes into the space or runs at its opening' during the work. But steps[10].hazards names the hazard as 'Vapour in the explosive range set off by something the crew brought in — a head torch, a battery tool, the sump pump or its lead, THE BLOWER MOTOR, or static off a spray gun or a drum', and steps[6] is where the blower motor and its starter are switched on. steps[6].controls[4] positions the blower intake for carbon monoxide only. In the same step steps[6].controls[9] has a torch lighting the space from outside, and steps[7] then puts a sampling hose and probe down it — all before a reading. It also contradicts steps[1].controls[2]: 'Whenever the opening is open — entry or not — the space is signed under s 68, hard-guarded, and the atmosphere is tested from outside.' A wet well with the sewer cross-connection named at steps[7].hazards, or a tank with a lining history, is at its worst on the first crack of the lid, which is precisely the moment this document has no number and a non-Ex motor running at the hatch.
blocking.fix: Reorder steps[6]: take the first atmospheric reading from outside BEFORE the blower is started — that reading is what tells you whether the blower, the torch and the instruments can be used at all — then purge and retest, and change the wording to 'purge for at least 20 minutes before the ENTRY test'. Add an ignition control to steps[6] at 'substitute' or 'isolate' level: where that first reading is not a clean zero on LEL, or the space has any flammable history under steps[1].controls[6] and siteSpecificPrompts[31], the blower is air-driven or its motor and starter are certified and kept out of what is venting from the opening, and the torch and instruments are intrinsically safe — Work Health and Safety Regulation 2011 (Qld) s 73 applies from the moment the lid moves, not from the moment the work starts.

blocking.field: steps[4].controls[1] (level "engineering") — "Where the vent cannot be proven clear at all, open the hatch or a manway first so the tank has a second path to air before any water moves"
blocking.problem: THE DRAW-DOWN STEP SENDS THE CREW TO CRACK A HATCH ON A FULL TANK, THREE STEPS BEFORE THE CONTROLS THAT KEEP THEM OUT OF IT. The words 'before any water moves' fix the moment: the tank is still full. Opening a hatch over full water is the single scenario steps[6].controls[10] was written for — 'Harness on and connected to a restraint line from a rated anchor BEFORE the lid moves on any tank or well holding water — the person cracking a hatch over full water is standing at an open edge with nothing else on them yet, and the permit controls do not exist at that moment' — and steps[6].controls[0] requires the opening hard-guarded 'BEFORE anyone puts their head over it', with steps[6].controls[7] adding the upwind rule and the propped lid. steps[4] carries none of that and makes no cross-reference, so a crew reading down opens a hatch over several metres of water with no guard, no restraint line, no upwind rule and no lid prop. The omission is inconsistent inside a single control: the same steps[4].controls[1] does point forward correctly for the vent check — 'that check happens on the rated access in the next step and the drain valve does not open until it is done' — so the author handled the sequencing for the vent and not for the hatch.
blocking.fix: In steps[4].controls[1], give the hatch-opening fallback the same forward pointer the vent check already has: the hatch is not cracked to give the tank a second air path until the rated access of steps[5] is in place and the hard guard, the restraint line off a rated anchor, the upwind rule and the propped lid of steps[6].controls[0], [7] and [10] are in place. Add 'opening a hatch on a full tank to give it an air path, before any of the opening controls exist' to steps[4].hazards.

blocking.problem: Two restoration procedures labelled engineering, which pushes the step's real hold point down to fourth. steps[12].controls[1] reads in full: 'Refill the tank and watch the fill. A ball float valve that sticks is a defect found now or a flood found later.' Watching a fill is a person paying attention — administrative. steps[12].controls[2] ('Restore the pumpset properly: batteries on, fuel valve open, auto-start pressure switch back in service, controller to AUTO, then prove it with a test start') is a sequence of operations and a functional check — also administrative. Because the ordering rule ranks by level, both sit above steps[12].controls[3], which is the one control in the step that stops a building being handed back unprotected: 'HOLD POINT — the system is not handed back and the impairment is not closed until the tank level is confirmed at or above the design low-water level AND the pumpset has proven in AUTO on a test start.' steps[12].controls[0] is correctly engineering — strapping or locking the suction valve open is a physical control that survives the crew leaving.
blocking.fix: Relabel steps[12].controls[1] and steps[12].controls[2] to 'administrative' and move the hold point up so the step reads: strapped-open suction valve (engineering), then the hold point, then the refill and the pumpset restoration under it.

blocking.field: steps[10].hazards ("Biological contamination — bird droppings, algae, legionella in warm stagnant water, leptospirosis in pits"), with steps[10].controls[11] and steps[10].controls[12]
blocking.problem: Legionella is named and only the wrong route is controlled. Legionella is inhaled as an aerosol; it is not a hand-to-mouth infection. The controls offered are steps[10].controls[12] — 'Coveralls, nitrile gloves and eye protection where there is sludge, bird droppings or algae. Wash hands and face before eating' — which are the leptospirosis and contact controls, and steps[10].controls[11], which scopes respiratory protection to 'wherever coatings, scale or rust are disturbed or the work generates vapour or dust'. That scope misses every aerosol-generating act this job actually performs: the sump pump running for the whole entry at steps[10].controls[4], hosing or squeegeeing sludge, and the blower at steps[6].controls[3] blasting air across warm standing water at the bottom of the space. A fire tank that has sat part-full through a Queensland summer is the textbook growth condition, and the entrant is breathing the plume in an enclosed space.
blocking.fix: Extend steps[10].controls[11] to name aerosol as well as dust and vapour: respiratory protection selected under AS/NZS 1715:2009 wherever water is being pumped, hosed or agitated in a space that has held warm stagnant water, not only where coatings, scale or rust are disturbed. Add to steps[10].controls[4] that the sump discharge is run away from the opening so the standby is not standing in the plume.

blocking.field: steps[0].controls[5] ("Confirm the crew is three...") and the training array
blocking.problem: The document checks the tickets and the gear and never checks the person. steps[0].controls[4] runs the harness, straps, line, tripod and winch through your hands for cuts, corrosion and heat glazing; steps[0].controls[5] confirms RIIWHS202E, PUASAR025 and MSMWHS217; the ppe array requires a current fit test and a clean-shaven sealing surface. Nothing asks whether the entrant or the standby is fit to do this today: heart or respiratory condition, medication, injury, illness, fatigue, or claustrophobia in a 600mm hatch, and on the standby's side the physical capacity to wind a limp adult up six metres of line alone. steps[0].controls[8] rules out the end of a long shift, which is the closest the document comes, and steps[10].controls[8] gives an unacclimatised worker half rotations — so the author already accepts that the individual, not just the space, decides the risk.
blocking.fix: Add an administrative control to steps[0], beside the crew check: before the crew is confirmed, the entrant and the standby each declare fitness for this entry — health condition, medication, injury, illness, fatigue — and anyone who is not fit does not enter and does not stand by; the job is recrewed or rescheduled, not covered by watching them. Tie the standby's physical capacity to steps[8].controls[7], which already requires them to demonstrate a loaded retrieval on the rigged winch before the first entry of the day.

blocking.problem: The file ships carrying the previous round's verdict against itself. The shipped JSON contains "review": {"cleared": false, "reason": "A reviewer read the corrected statement and would not sign it.", "findings": [...]} and the two findings it lists are the ignition-source omission and the structural-assessment omission — both of which THIS version answers, at steps[10].controls[0] and steps[10].controls[3] and across the whole of the new steps[4]. It is stale metadata the correction did not clear. If any of it reaches a screen in the app, a technician standing at a hatch is told the statement in their hand was refused, over two faults it no longer has, which is exactly the kind of thing that teaches a crew to ignore the banner next time it is true.
blocking.fix: Regenerate or clear the top-level "review" object as part of the correction so it reflects the version it ships with, and make sure the app does not surface a stale review state on a current statement.
